name: test

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  pytest:
    name: pytest (${{ matrix.os }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, windows-latest]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.14"
      - name: Get Hermes
        shell: bash
        run: |
          git config --global core.longpaths true
          git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent.git "$RUNNER_TEMP/hermes-agent"
      - name: Install Hermes, the plugin and its tests
        shell: bash
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          python -m pip install -e "$RUNNER_TEMP/hermes-agent"
          python -m pip install -e ".[test]"
      - name: Show which PowerShell and bash the Windows tests will use
        shell: bash
        run: |
          command -v pwsh || true
          command -v powershell || true
          command -v bash
      - name: Run the tests
        run: python -m pytest -q -rs

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[project]
name = "hermes-cua-spaces"
version = "0.2.0"
description = "Hermes Agent terminal backend that runs commands inside a Cua Space (Linux, macOS or Windows)"
readme = "README.md"
license = { text = "MIT" }
authors = [{ name = "Cua", email = "hello@trycua.com" }]
requires-python = ">=3.11"
dependencies = ["cua>=0.5.0,<0.6"]

[project.optional-dependencies]
test = ["pytest"]

[project.urls]
Homepage = "https://github.com/trycua/hermes-cua-spaces"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["hermes_cua_spaces"]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]

# Hermes on Cua Spaces

Run Hermes Agent's terminal, file and code tools inside a [Cua Space](https://cua.ai/spaces): an isolated machine you can watch live, on your own hardware or in your own cloud account.

Hermes still runs where it runs today. When it needs to run a command, write a file or execute code, that work happens in the Space instead of on your computer. Because the Space is the sandbox, Hermes skips its risky-command prompts for Spaces this plugin creates.

Hermes users: get your first month of Cua Spaces Pro or Teams free with code `HERMES-3EPX2A` (first 50, until 15 Nov).

```
you  ->  Hermes (your machine)  ->  this plugin  ->  Cua Space (an isolated Linux, macOS or Windows machine)
                                                      terminal, files, code run here
```

## Install in 3 steps

1. Install Cua and sign in (sign-in is only needed for Spaces on your cua.ai account; a local Space needs none):

   ```bash
   curl -fsSL https://cua.ai/install.sh | sh
   cua auth login
   ```

2. Install the plugin:

   ```bash
   hermes plugins install https://github.com/trycua/hermes-cua-spaces
   ```

   Hermes asks to install one Python package (`cua`). Say yes, and say yes to enabling the plugin.

3. Point Hermes at it:

   ```bash
   hermes config set terminal.backend cua
   ```

Start Hermes as usual. The first command creates a Space (the first one takes a few minutes while Cua downloads the machine image). After that, every terminal command, file read, file write and code run lands in the Space.

Check it worked by asking Hermes: `run hostname and cat /etc/os-release`. You will see the Space's name and Ubuntu, not your own computer. On a Windows Space ask for `hostname` and `(Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem).Caption`.

## Settings

The plugin keeps its settings in Hermes's `config.yaml`, under `plugins.entries.cua-spaces.settings`. Set them with `hermes config set`.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `space` | `create` | `create` makes a Space for you. Or give the name or id of a Space you already have, for example `my-box`. |
| `on` | your Cua default | Where a new Space goes: `local`, `cloud`, `host:<machine>`, or the name of one of your machines. |
| `image` | `linux` | The image for a new Space. `linux` is Ubuntu with a desktop. `windows` makes a Windows Space (see [Windows Spaces](#windows-spaces)). |
| `delete_on_exit` | `true` | Delete a Space the plugin created when Hermes finishes. Set `false` to keep it for next time. A Space you named is never deleted. |
| `create_timeout` | `600` | Seconds to wait for a new Space to be ready. |

Examples:

```bash
# use a Space you already made
hermes config set plugins.entries.cua-spaces.settings.space my-box

# make new Spaces on another of your machines
hermes config set plugins.entries.cua-spaces.settings.on "spare mac mini"
```

The environment variables `HERMES_CUA_SPACE`, `HERMES_CUA_ON` and `HERMES_CUA_IMAGE` override the same settings for one shell.

How the plugin picks a Space:

- `space: create` (the default): each Hermes run makes its own Space, named `hermes-<task>-<random>`, does the work there and deletes it when it finishes. Two Hermes runs at once get two Spaces and never touch each other's files.
- `space: create` and `delete_on_exit: false`: the plugin makes one Space called `hermes-default` the first time and reuses it after that, so your files are still there next session. It stays running when Hermes exits. Stop it with `cua spaces stop hermes-default` or delete it with `cua spaces delete hermes-default`.
- `space: my-box`: the plugin uses that Space and never deletes or stops it. Because it is your machine and not a throwaway one, Hermes keeps asking before risky commands.

### Sign-in and keys

The plugin never stores a token or key. It talks to Cua through the `cua` Python package, which uses the sign-in that `cua auth login` saved. Nothing about Cua goes in `config.yaml` or `.env`.

### Working folder

Leave `terminal.cwd` alone. A new session starts in the Space user's home folder (`/home/cua` on Linux, `C:\Users\<name>` on Windows). If you ask Hermes to create files, use absolute paths such as `/home/cua/project/app.py` or `C:\Users\cua\project\app.py`.

## Watch the Space live

Open the Cua Spaces app and click the Space (`hermes-default`, or the one you named). You see its desktop as Hermes works. In a terminal, `cua spaces ls` lists your Spaces and `cua viewer` serves a browser viewer for all of them. You can click in the viewer to take over; Hermes keeps working next to you.

## Run several in parallel

Give each Hermes its own Space.

- Separate Hermes profiles, each with its own Space:

  ```bash
  HERMES_CUA_SPACE=build-a hermes --profile a
  HERMES_CUA_SPACE=build-b hermes --profile b
  ```

  `build-a` and `build-b` must exist (create them with `cua spaces create linux --name build-a`).

- Throwaway Spaces, one per run: this is the default. Every Hermes you start makes its own Space and deletes it when it finishes, so you can start as many as your machine can hold.

## Two other ways to use Cua with Hermes

These work today and need no plugin.

**1. Give Hermes the Cua tools (`cua mcp`).** Hermes can then create Spaces, run commands in them, drive their desktops and delete them, as tools it calls itself. Add this to `~/.hermes/config.yaml`:

```yaml
mcp_servers:
  cua:
    command: cua
    args: ["mcp"]
```

Limit what Hermes may do with `--permissions` (for example `args: ["mcp", "--permissions", "spaces:readonly"]`) and with `tools.include` in the same block.

**2. Run Hermes itself inside a Space.** Everything stays in the Space: the agent, its keys and its tools.

```bash
cua agent create ada --harness hermes --in local:dev --env-from-host OPENAI_API_KEY
cua agent tell ada "summarize the repo in /home/cua/project"
```

Hermes keeps its memory in your Cua Volume, so it survives if the Space is replaced.

## Windows Spaces

Windows Spaces are new in 0.2.0. Point the plugin at a Windows Space you have, or make one:

```bash
cua spaces create windows --name my-pc
hermes config set plugins.entries.cua-spaces.settings.space my-pc
# or let the plugin make one for each run
hermes config set plugins.entries.cua-spaces.settings.image windows
```

The first Windows Space takes a while to create while Cua downloads the machine image. A Windows Space on an Apple silicon Mac runs by emulation and is slow; use a Windows Space on an x86 machine or in your cloud account for real work.

Hermes was written for a Unix shell, so a few tools behave differently on Windows:

| Hermes tool | On a Windows Space |
|---|---|
| `terminal` | Runs in PowerShell: `pwsh` (PowerShell 7) if the Space has it, otherwise the `powershell.exe` that ships with Windows. Write PowerShell, not bash: `Get-ChildItem`, not `ls -la`. Hermes tells the model this. The folder you `cd` into is remembered between commands. A command's exit code is the last command's: a failing program's own exit code, `1` for a PowerShell error, or the number in `exit N`. Output is UTF-8. |
| File tools: read, write, patch | Work on Windows paths (`C:\Users\cua\app.py`, `C:/Users/cua/app.py` or `~\app.py`). A relative path starts from the terminal's current folder. Files keep their line endings (LF or CRLF) and byte-order mark. |
| File search | Needs Git for Windows in the Space (it brings `bash`, `grep` and `find`). Without it the tool says so, in plain words, and nothing else is affected. |
| Background processes, `execute_code` | Run Unix shell commands. They use Git for Windows' bash when the Space has it, and say what to install when it doesn't. |
| Browser tools, `computer_use` | Same as other Spaces: not in the Space yet. |

To turn on the Unix-shell tools, install Git for Windows in the Space, from its PowerShell: `winget install --id Git.Git -e`. Hermes finds it next time it connects.

If a Space cannot start PowerShell, the plugin says so and names the Space. Linux and macOS Spaces are unchanged.

## What does and does not run in the Space

| | In the Space with this plugin |
|---|---|
| `terminal` tool, background processes | yes |
| File tools (read, write, patch, search) | yes |
| `execute_code` | yes |
| Browser tools, `computer_use`, Bot Desktop | no, not yet. They still use your own machine (see below) |

Hermes only lets `computer_use` and Bot Desktop follow the built-in `docker`, `ssh` and `singularity` backends. Following a plugin backend needs a small change in Hermes. It is proposed to Nous. Until it lands, use the second option above (Hermes inside a Space) if you want the desktop to live in the Space.

## What the plugin does and sends

- It calls the Cua SDK to create, find, start and delete Spaces, and to run commands and write files in them.
- With a local Space, nothing leaves your machine. With a Space on another machine or your cloud account, commands and files go through Cua's encrypted relay or your own network.
- It does not sync your Hermes skills, cache or credentials into the Space. The Space starts with what its image has.
- It adds no telemetry. The `cua` package has its own anonymous usage telemetry; turn it off with `cua telemetry off` or `CUA_TELEMETRY=0`.

## When something goes wrong

The plugin explains errors in plain words and says what to run next. The most common ones:

| You see | Do this |
|---|---|
| "Cua did not accept your sign-in" | `cua auth login` |
| "Cua can't find the Space ..." | `cua spaces ls`, then fix the `space` setting or use `create` |
| "Cua can't start a Space here yet" | `cua doctor` shows what is missing |
| "The `cua` Python package is not installed" | `hermes pm repair` |
| "This Hermes tool runs Unix shell commands, and this Windows Space has no Unix shell" | Install Git for Windows in the Space: `winget install --id Git.Git -e`. Or use the terminal tool, which works without it |
| "Could not start PowerShell in the Windows Space ..." | Check the Space is running (`cua spaces ls`) and that `powershell.exe` runs in it |

## Develop

```bash
uv venv --python 3.14 && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e ".[test]" hermes-agent
pytest
hermes plugins validate . --install-deps
```

The tests run the whole environment against a local shell standing in for a Space, so they need no Cua account. The Windows tests use PowerShell 7 (`pwsh`) as the stand-in and skip themselves when it is missing; on a Windows machine they run in real Windows PowerShell. CI runs them on Linux, macOS and Windows.

## Licence

MIT, the same as the Cua SDKs. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).

import pytest

pytest.importorskip("agent.terminal_env_provider", reason="needs Hermes installed")

import hermes_cua_spaces as plugin  # noqa: E402


def test_provider_shape():
    p = plugin.CuaSpacesProvider()
    assert p.name == "cua" and p.is_remote and p.is_container
    assert "CUA_API_KEY" in p.strip_env_keys
    assert p.session_isolated_when_nonpersistent
    assert p.probe()[0] in ("ready", "needs_setup")
    assert all(len(row) == 3 for row in p.doctor_checks())


def test_guards_skipped_only_for_spaces_we_create():
    creating = plugin.CuaSpacesProvider(get_config=lambda k, default=None: default)
    assert creating.skip_container_guards is True
    named = plugin.CuaSpacesProvider(get_config=lambda k, default=None: "my-box" if k == "space" else default)
    assert named.skip_container_guards is False


def test_register_wires_provider():
    seen = []

    class Ctx:
        def register_terminal_environment_provider(self, p):
            seen.append(p)

    plugin.register(Ctx())
    assert len(seen) == 1 and seen[0].name == "cua"


def test_create_environment_passes_persistence(client):
    p = plugin.CuaSpacesProvider(get_config=lambda k, default=None: default, client=client)
    env = p.create_environment(cwd="/root", timeout=10, task_id="a", container_config={"container_persistent": False})
    env.cleanup()
    assert client.deleted == [client.space.id]

"""The Hermes environment, driven end to end against a local shell standing in for the Space."""
import pytest

pytest.importorskip("tools.environments.base", reason="needs Hermes installed")

from hermes_cua_spaces.config import Settings  # noqa: E402
from hermes_cua_spaces.environment import CuaSpaceEnvironment  # noqa: E402


def make(client, **kw):
    args = dict(cwd="/root", timeout=30, task_id="t1", settings=Settings(), client=client, persistent=True)
    args.update(kw)
    return CuaSpaceEnvironment(**args)


def test_runs_command_and_returns_output(client):
    env = make(client)
    r = env.execute("echo hello && echo oops 1>&2")
    assert r["returncode"] == 0
    assert "hello" in r["output"] and "oops" in r["output"]
    env.cleanup()


def test_exit_code(client):
    env = make(client)
    assert env.execute("exit 7")["returncode"] == 7
    env.cleanup()


def test_default_cwd_is_space_home_not_root(client, space):
    env = make(client, cwd="/root")
    assert env.cwd == str(space.root)
    assert env.execute("pwd")["output"].strip() == str(space.root)
    env.cleanup()


def test_cwd_and_env_persist_between_commands(client, space):
    env = make(client)
    (space.root / "sub").mkdir()
    env.execute("cd sub && export FOO=bar")
    out = env.execute("pwd; echo $FOO")["output"]
    assert out.splitlines()[0].endswith("/sub") and out.splitlines()[1] == "bar"
    env.cleanup()


def test_stdin_data_is_delivered_exactly(client, space):
    env = make(client)
    payload = "no trailing newline é"
    r = env.execute("cat > out.txt", stdin_data=payload)
    assert r["returncode"] == 0
    assert (space.root / "out.txt").read_bytes() == payload.encode()
    env.cleanup()


def test_timeout_is_reported(client):
    env = make(client, timeout=1)
    r = env.execute("sleep 5", timeout=1)
    assert r["returncode"] == 124
    env.cleanup()


def test_create_mode_uses_task_name_and_settings(client):
    env = make(client, task_id="Session 9", settings=Settings(image="linux", on="local"))
    assert client.calls[0][:1] == ("ensure",) and client.calls[0][1].startswith("hermes-session-9-")
    assert client.calls[0][2:] == ("linux", "local")
    env.cleanup()


def test_named_space_is_attached_and_never_deleted(client):
    env = make(client, settings=Settings(space="my-box"), persistent=False)
    assert client.calls[0] == ("attach", "my-box")
    env.cleanup()
    assert client.deleted == []


def test_created_space_deleted_by_default_and_kept_when_asked(client):
    make(client, settings=Settings(delete_on_exit=False), persistent=True).cleanup()
    assert client.deleted == []
    assert client.calls[-1][1] == "hermes-t1"  # kept Spaces have a stable name
    env = make(client, persistent=True)
    env.cleanup()
    assert client.deleted == [client.space.id]
    client.deleted.clear()
    env = make(client, settings=Settings(delete_on_exit=False), persistent=False)
    env.cleanup()
    env.cleanup()  # idempotent
    assert client.deleted == [client.space.id]


def test_space_error_becomes_readable_output(client, space):
    from hermes_cua_spaces.errors import CuaSpacesError

    env = make(client)

    def broken(command, timeout_s):
        raise CuaSpacesError("The Space is gone. Check `cua spaces ls`.")

    space.run = broken
    r = env.execute("echo hi")
    assert r["returncode"] != 0 and "Cua Space error" in r["output"] and "cua spaces ls" in r["output"]

"""SdkSpacesClient against a fake `cua` module (no network, no real Space)."""
import asyncio
import sys
import types

import pytest

from hermes_cua_spaces.config import Settings
from hermes_cua_spaces.errors import NotSignedInError, SpaceCreateError


class Info:
    def __init__(self, name, os="linux", power="running"):
        self.id, self.name, self.os, self.power_state, self.power = f"local:{name}", name, os, power, power


class FakeBash:
    def __init__(self, **kw):
        base = dict(stdout="", stderr="", exit_code=0, signal=None, timed_out=False, error=None)
        base.update(kw)
        self.__dict__.update(base)


class FakeSpace:
    def __init__(self, result):
        self.result, self.commands, self.writes = result, [], []

    async def bash(self, command, timeout_ms):
        self.commands.append((command, timeout_ms))
        if isinstance(self.result, Exception):
            raise self.result
        return self.result

    async def write(self, path, data):
        self.writes.append((path, data))

    async def home(self):
        return "/home/cua"


class FakeSpaces:
    def __init__(self):
        self.infos, self.spaces, self.created, self.deleted, self.started = {}, {}, [], [], []

    async def resolve(self, name):
        if name in self.infos:
            return self.infos[name]
        for info in self.infos.values():
            if info.id == name:
                return info
        raise type("NotFound", (Exception,), {})(f"not found: {name}")

    async def space(self, sid):
        return self.spaces.setdefault(sid, FakeSpace(FakeBash(stdout="hi\n")))

    async def create(self, options):
        info = Info(options.name)
        self.created.append(options)
        self.infos[options.name] = info
        return types.SimpleNamespace(space=info, pending_id=None, reused=False)

    async def start(self, sid):
        self.started.append(sid)

    async def delete(self, sid):
        self.deleted.append(sid)
        return "deleted"


@pytest.fixture
def sdk(monkeypatch):
    spaces = FakeSpaces()
    mod = types.ModuleType("cua")
    runtime = types.SimpleNamespace(spaces=lambda: spaces)
    mod.CuaConfig = type("CuaConfig", (), {"__init__": lambda self, *, fleet_from_session=False: None})
    mod.Cua = types.SimpleNamespace(auto=lambda config: runtime)
    mod.SpaceCreateOptions = lambda **kw: types.SimpleNamespace(**kw)
    monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules, "cua", mod)
    from hermes_cua_spaces.client import SdkSpacesClient

    return SdkSpacesClient(), spaces


def test_uses_cua_login_session_flag(sdk):
    client, _ = sdk
    assert client._session_kwargs(sys.modules["cua"]) == {"fleet_from_session": True}


def test_ensure_creates_once_then_reuses(sdk):
    client, spaces = sdk
    s = Settings(image="linux", on="local")
    h, created = client.ensure("hermes-a", s)
    assert created and h.name == "hermes-a"
    assert (spaces.created[0].image, spaces.created[0].on, spaces.created[0].wait) == ("linux", "local", True)
    h2, created2 = client.ensure("hermes-a", s)
    assert not created2 and len(spaces.created) == 1


def test_default_location_passes_none(sdk):
    client, spaces = sdk
    client.ensure("hermes-b", Settings())
    assert spaces.created[0].on is None


def test_attach_missing_space_is_plain(sdk):
    client, _ = sdk
    with pytest.raises(Exception) as err:
        client.attach("ghost")
    assert "cua spaces ls" in str(err.value)


def test_attach_starts_stopped_space(sdk):
    client, spaces = sdk
    spaces.infos["old"] = Info("old", power="stopped")
    client.attach("old")
    assert spaces.started == ["local:old"]


def test_windows_space_is_attached(sdk):
    client, spaces = sdk
    spaces.infos["win"] = Info("win", os="windows")
    handle = client.attach("win")
    assert handle.os == "windows"


def test_linux_space_reports_its_os(sdk):
    client, spaces = sdk
    spaces.infos["lin"] = Info("lin")
    assert client.attach("lin").os == "linux"


def test_run_merges_streams_and_maps_codes(sdk):
    client, spaces = sdk
    spaces.infos["x"] = Info("x")
    h = client.attach("x")
    sp = spaces.spaces["local:x"]
    sp.result = FakeBash(stdout="out\n", stderr="err\n", exit_code=3)
    r = h.run("cmd", 5)
    assert (r.output, r.exit_code) == ("out\nerr\n", 3)
    assert sp.commands[-1] == ("cmd", 5000)
    sp.result = FakeBash(exit_code=None, timed_out=True)
    assert h.run("cmd", 1).exit_code == 124
    sp.result = FakeBash(exit_code=None, signal="KILL")
    assert h.run("cmd", 1).exit_code == 137


def test_run_error_is_explained(sdk):
    client, spaces = sdk
    spaces.infos["x"] = Info("x")
    h = client.attach("x")
    spaces.spaces["local:x"].result = type("Unauthenticated", (Exception,), {})("nope")
    with pytest.raises(NotSignedInError):
        h.run("cmd", 1)


def test_create_without_space_result_is_plain(sdk):
    client, spaces = sdk

    async def pending(options):
        return types.SimpleNamespace(space=None, pending_id="p1", reused=False)

    spaces.create = pending
    with pytest.raises(SpaceCreateError, match="still being created"):
        client.ensure("hermes-slow", Settings())


def test_delete(sdk):
    client, spaces = sdk
    client.delete("local:x")
    assert spaces.deleted == ["local:x"]

"""Directory-install entry point for Hermes.

`hermes plugins install` copies this repository into `~/.hermes/plugins/cua-spaces/`
and loads this file. The code lives in the `hermes_cua_spaces` package next to it, so put
this directory on `sys.path` and re-export `register`.
"""

import os
import sys

_HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
if _HERE not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, _HERE)

from hermes_cua_spaces import CuaSpacesProvider, register  # noqa: E402,F401

__all__ = ["CuaSpacesProvider", "register"]

name: cua-spaces
version: "0.2.0"
manifest_version: 2
description: Run Hermes terminal, file and code tools inside a Cua Space (an isolated Linux, macOS or Windows machine you can watch live).
author: Cua
kind: backend
license: MIT
homepage: https://github.com/trycua/hermes-cua-spaces
tags: [terminal, sandbox, cua]
python_dependencies:
  - "cua>=0.5.0,<0.6"
provides_tools: []
provides_hooks: []
capabilities: []
config_schema:
  space:
    type: str
    default: create
    label: Space
    description: "'create' makes a Space for you. Or give the name or id of a Space that already exists."
  on:
    type: str
    default: ""
    label: Where
    description: "local, cloud, host:<machine> or a machine name. Empty uses your Cua default."
  image:
    type: str
    default: linux
    label: Image
    description: "Image for a new Space: linux, or any image name Cua accepts."
  create_timeout:
    type: int
    default: 600
    label: Create timeout (seconds)
    description: "How long to wait for a new Space to be ready."
  delete_on_exit:
    type: bool
    default: true
    label: Delete the Space when Hermes finishes
    description: "Applies only to Spaces the plugin creates. A Space you name is never deleted."

"""One background event loop for the async Cua SDK.

Hermes runs tools on plain threads and the Cua SDK is async, so every SDK call goes through a single
loop that lives on its own daemon thread. That also lets many Hermes sessions share one SDK runtime.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import threading
from concurrent.futures import TimeoutError as FutureTimeout
from typing import Any, Coroutine, Optional, TypeVar

T = TypeVar("T")

_lock = threading.Lock()
_loop: Optional[asyncio.AbstractEventLoop] = None


def _get_loop() -> asyncio.AbstractEventLoop:
    global _loop
    with _lock:
        if _loop is not None and _loop.is_running():
            return _loop
        loop = asyncio.new_event_loop()
        ready = threading.Event()

        def run() -> None:
            asyncio.set_event_loop(loop)
            loop.call_soon(ready.set)
            loop.run_forever()

        threading.Thread(target=run, name="hermes-cua-spaces", daemon=True).start()
        ready.wait(5)
        _loop = loop
        return loop


def run_sync(coro: Coroutine[Any, Any, T], timeout: Optional[float] = None) -> T:
    """Run a coroutine on the shared loop and wait for it. Raises TimeoutError on timeout."""
    future = asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe(coro, _get_loop())
    try:
        return future.result(timeout)
    except FutureTimeout:
        future.cancel()
        raise TimeoutError("timed out waiting for Cua") from None

"""Hermes terminal backend that runs commands inside a Cua Space.

    hermes plugins install https://github.com/trycua/hermes-cua-spaces
    hermes config set terminal.backend cua

Sign in once with `cua auth login` (only needed for Spaces on your cua.ai account; a local Space
needs no sign-in).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import importlib.util
import shutil
import threading
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Tuple

from agent.terminal_env_provider import TerminalEnvironmentProvider

from . import windows, windows_files
from .config import Settings, load_settings
from .errors import CuaSpacesError

__version__ = "0.2.0"

_client_lock = threading.Lock()
_client: Any = None


def _shared_client() -> Any:
    """One SDK runtime for the whole Hermes process, made on first use."""
    global _client
    with _client_lock:
        if _client is None:
            from .client import SdkSpacesClient

            _client = SdkSpacesClient()
        return _client


class CuaSpacesProvider(TerminalEnvironmentProvider):
    name = "cua"
    display_name = "Cua Spaces"
    is_remote = True
    is_container = True
    # With `terminal.container_persistent: false` each Hermes session gets its own Space,
    # so several Hermes runs in parallel never share one machine by accident.
    session_isolated_when_nonpersistent = True

    def __init__(self, get_config: Any = None, client: Any = None) -> None:
        self._get_config = get_config
        self._client_override = client
        self._windows_seen = False

    # -- what Hermes shows and decides on --
    @property
    def description(self) -> str:
        return "Run terminal, file and code tools inside a Cua Space, an isolated machine you can watch live."

    @property
    def env_description(self) -> str:
        if self._windows_seen:
            return f"a Cua Space (an isolated Windows machine). {windows.TERMINAL_NOTE}"
        return "a Cua Space (an isolated Linux, macOS or Windows machine)"

    @property
    def skip_container_guards(self) -> bool:
        # A Space we create is a disposable sandbox, so Hermes can skip risky-command prompts.
        # A Space you point us at is your own machine: keep the prompts.
        try:
            return load_settings(self._get_config).creates
        except Exception:
            return False

    @property
    def strip_env_keys(self) -> frozenset:
        return frozenset({"CUA_API_KEY", "CUA_DAEMON_TOKEN"})

    def is_available(self) -> bool:
        return importlib.util.find_spec("cua") is not None

    def probe(self) -> Tuple[str, str]:
        if not self.is_available():
            return ("needs_setup", "The cua Python package is not installed. Run `hermes pm repair`.")
        return ("ready", "")

    def setup_instructions(self) -> List[str]:
        return [
            "hermes config set terminal.backend cua",
            "Optional: cua auth login   (only for Spaces on your cua.ai account)",
            "Optional: hermes config set plugins.entries.cua-spaces.settings.space my-space",
            "Watch the Space live: open the Cua Spaces app, or run `cua spaces ls`.",
        ]

    def doctor_checks(self) -> List[Tuple[bool, str, str]]:
        sdk = self.is_available()
        cli = shutil.which("cua") is not None
        return [
            (sdk, "Cua Python SDK", "(installed)" if sdk else "(missing: run `hermes pm repair`)"),
            (cli, "cua command", "(found)" if cli else "(not on PATH: optional, install from https://cua.ai)"),
        ]

    def create_environment(
        self,
        *,
        cwd: str,
        timeout: int,
        task_id: str = "default",
        image: Optional[str] = None,
        container_config: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
        **kwargs: Any,
    ):
        from .environment import CuaSpaceEnvironment

        settings: Settings = load_settings(self._get_config)
        persistent = bool((container_config or {}).get("container_persistent", True))
        client = self._client_override or _shared_client()
        env = CuaSpaceEnvironment(
            cwd=cwd, timeout=timeout, task_id=task_id, settings=settings, client=client, persistent=persistent
        )
        if env.is_windows:
            self._windows_seen = True
            windows_files.install()
        return env


def register(ctx) -> None:
    """Plugin entry point."""
    get_config = getattr(ctx, "get_config", None)
    windows_files.install()
    ctx.register_terminal_environment_provider(CuaSpacesProvider(get_config=get_config))


__all__ = ["CuaSpacesProvider", "CuaSpacesError", "register", "__version__"]

"""Plugin settings. No secrets live here: sign-in comes from `cua auth login`."""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import re
import uuid
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any, Callable, Mapping, Optional

CREATE = "create"
DEFAULT_IMAGE = "linux"
DEFAULT_CREATE_TIMEOUT_S = 600

# Environment variables win over config.yaml, so one shell can point Hermes at a different Space.
ENV_SPACE = "HERMES_CUA_SPACE"
ENV_ON = "HERMES_CUA_ON"
ENV_IMAGE = "HERMES_CUA_IMAGE"
ENV_KEEP = "HERMES_CUA_KEEP"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Settings:
    """What the user chose.

    space   "create" makes a Space; anything else names (or gives the id of) an existing one.
    on      where to create: "local", "cloud", "host:<machine>" or a machine name. "" = Cua default.
    image   image for a new Space.
    """

    space: str = CREATE
    on: str = ""
    image: str = DEFAULT_IMAGE
    create_timeout_s: int = DEFAULT_CREATE_TIMEOUT_S
    # Delete a Space this plugin created when the Hermes session ends. Never applies to a Space you named.
    delete_on_exit: bool = True

    @property
    def creates(self) -> bool:
        return self.space.strip().lower() == CREATE

    def validate(self) -> "Settings":
        if not self.space.strip():
            raise ValueError("The Space setting is empty. Use `create` or the name of a Space.")
        if self.create_timeout_s <= 0:
            raise ValueError("create_timeout must be a positive number of seconds.")
        return self


def load_settings(
    get_config: Optional[Callable[..., Any]] = None,
    environ: Optional[Mapping[str, str]] = None,
) -> Settings:
    """Read settings from Hermes plugin config (`get_config(key, default=...)`), then the environment."""
    env = os.environ if environ is None else environ

    def cfg(key: str, default: Any) -> Any:
        if get_config is None:
            return default
        try:
            value = get_config(key, default=default)
        except Exception:  # a broken config read must not stop the backend from loading
            return default
        return default if value is None else value

    space = str(env.get(ENV_SPACE) or cfg("space", CREATE)).strip()
    on = str(env.get(ENV_ON) or cfg("on", "")).strip()
    image = str(env.get(ENV_IMAGE) or cfg("image", DEFAULT_IMAGE)).strip() or DEFAULT_IMAGE
    try:
        timeout = int(cfg("create_timeout", DEFAULT_CREATE_TIMEOUT_S))
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        timeout = DEFAULT_CREATE_TIMEOUT_S
    keep_env = str(env.get(ENV_KEEP) or "").strip().lower()
    if keep_env:
        delete = keep_env not in ("1", "true", "yes", "on")
    else:
        raw = cfg("delete_on_exit", True)
        delete = raw if isinstance(raw, bool) else str(raw).strip().lower() not in ("0", "false", "no", "off")
    return Settings(
        space=space or CREATE, on=on, image=image, create_timeout_s=timeout, delete_on_exit=delete
    ).validate()


_SAFE = re.compile(r"[^a-z0-9-]+")


def space_name_for(task_id: str, unique: bool = False) -> str:
    """A valid Space name for a Hermes task: `hermes-<task>`, plus a short random tag when `unique`.

    Unique names keep two Hermes runs from ever sharing (and deleting) one Space.
    """
    base = _SAFE.sub("-", f"{task_id or 'default'}".lower()).strip("-")[:24] or "default"
    name = f"hermes-{base}"
    return f"{name}-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]}" if unique else name
